body.statement: There exists \(\varepsilon>0\) such that, for every tuple \((\pi,(p_b)_{b=0}^{3},(\mu_b)_{b=0}^{3},(q_w)_{w=0}^{3})\in\Theta_3\) within \(\varepsilon\) in sup norm of \(\mathsf E_3\), every \(p_{bt}\) on \(\{0,1,2,3\}^2\) satisfying \(\sum_t p_{bt}=p_b\) and \(\sum_t t p_{bt}=\mu_b\), and menu \(\mathcal M=\{1,2,3\}\), the nontrivial Hall inequalities are strict, \(\mathcal V(p_{BT},q)\subsetneq\prod_{m\in\mathcal M}[\underline J_m,\overline J_m]\), \(D_{12}<D^{\Box}_{12}\), \(\mathcal M^\star=\{1\}\), and \(\mathcal M^{\Box}=\{3\}\). Here the shared-law quantities use the same-plan identities \(D_{mj}=\pi[\max_{x\in\Gamma_H(p,q)}\sum_{b=m}^{j-1}\sum_w w x_{bw}-\sum_{b=m}^{j-1}\mu_b]\) for \(m<j\), \(D_{mj}=\pi[\sum_{b=j}^{m-1}\mu_b-\min_{x\in\Gamma_H(p,q)}\sum_{b=j}^{m-1}\sum_w w x_{bw}]\) for \(m>j\), \(D_{mm}=0\), and \(R_m=\max_{j\in\mathcal M}D_{mj}\). Thus the shared-law regret rule is a strict joint-law tightening of applying the scalar sharp bounds of JanvinRyalenSarvetStensrud2025 threshold by threshold on a relatively open, nondegenerate family, with \(\mathsf E_3\) as one member.
body.justification: An open family establishes that common-law decision content is not a knife-edge numerical artifact of one rational table.
body.gap: JanvinRyalenSarvetStensrud2025 Proposition 1 supplies sharp scalar bounds and its decision section compares regimes using scalar-bound logic; it does not impose one latent transport law across a threshold menu, and on this family that omission strictly enlarges the payoff set and reverses the minimax threshold.
body.consumer: A trial analyst can diagnose when threshold-wise sharp intervals are insufficient for robust choice even though each reported scalar endpoint is individually correct.
